second_answer_attack.resolution: ABCB11 deficiency also causes low-GGT cholestasis, but it is an export defect after bile acids are synthesized. Low primary bile acids plus abundant atypical 3beta-hydroxy-delta5 intermediates demonstrate an HSD3B7 synthesis defect.

item.lead_in: Which hepatocyte transport process is most directly impaired?
item.tested_construct: ABCB11 encodes the bile salt export pump (BSEP), an ATP-binding cassette transporter on the canalicular membrane of hepatocytes that mediates biliary bile-acid export. BSEP deficiency causes PFIC2 with cholestasis and typically low or normal GGT.

blind_audit.rationale: HSD3B7 encodes a membrane-associated enzyme required early in bile-acid synthesis from cholesterol. Deficiency causes neonatal or infantile cholestatic liver disease with fat-soluble-vitamin malabsorption. A key biochemical clue is accumulation of atypical 3beta-hydroxy-delta5 bile-acid intermediates with deficient normal primary bile-acid production. Strongest alternative resolved: ABCB11 deficiency also causes low-GGT cholestasis, but it is an export defect after bile acids are synthesized. Low primary bile acids plus abundant atypical 3beta-hydroxy-delta5 intermediates demonstrate an HSD3B7 synthesis defect.
